title: Preparation of p-Nitroacetanilide
objective: Carry out the reaction under the specified conditions
Isolate the crude solid product by filtration/precipitation
Determine the melting point of the purified product as a purity check, and calculate the percentage yield

theory.statement: Acetanilide is nitrated with a cold mixture of concentrated nitric and sulphuric acids. The acetamido group is an ortho/para director but is deactivating enough (compared with a free amine) to allow controlled mononitration; the reaction is run cold and the major product is the para isomer, separated from the minor ortho isomer by recrystallisation.
theory.derivationNote: Crude yield is always higher than the yield after recrystallisation — the gap between the two is a direct, quantitative measure of the impurity removed in one recrystallisation. The melting point of the purified solid, sharp and close to the literature value, is the check that the removed material really was impurity and not product.

apparatus.name: Concentrated sulphuric acid
apparatus.why: Generates the nitronium ion (electrophile) from nitric acid, and moderates the reactivity of the ring

apparatus.name: Ice-salt freezing mixture
apparatus.why: Keeps the strongly exothermic nitration below about 5 °C, minimising oxidation and poly-nitration

procedure.text: Set up the reaction with the specified reagents, cooling as required for this exothermic step.
Once the reaction is complete, isolate the crude solid by filtration (or by pouring onto crushed ice, as appropriate).
Weigh the crude product and calculate the crude percentage yield.
Recrystallise from a suitable solvent, filter, and dry the purified crystals.
Determine the melting point of the purified product and compare with the literature value.

steps: Isolate and weigh the crude product; crude % yield
Determine the melting point as a purity check

expectedResult.quantity: Melting point of the purified product
expectedResult.statement: The crude product is obtained in good yield; recrystallisation lowers the yield but sharpens the melting point towards the literature value of about 214.0 °C, confirming the gain in purity.

safety: This nitration uses concentrated H2SO4 and HNO3 — highly corrosive; wear gloves and eye protection and work in a fume cupboard.
The reaction is strongly exothermic — add reagents slowly with continuous cooling.
Never add water to the concentrated acid mixture; if diluting, add acid to water, carefully, and only after the reaction.
sourcesOfError: Allowing the temperature to rise increases the proportion of the (harder-to-remove) ortho isomer and of oxidation products.
Adding the nitrating mixture too fast causes local overheating even in an ice bath.
Incomplete removal of the ortho isomer during recrystallisation lowers the measured melting point.

viva.question: Why must the acetanilide first be dissolved in concentrated H2SO4 rather than nitrated directly with HNO3?
viva.expectedConcept: Concentrated sulphuric acid protonates trace water and generates the nitronium ion, NO2+, the actual electrophile in nitration; it also keeps the amide from being oxidised or hydrolysed by moderating the reaction medium.
viva.answerLogic: H2SO4 generates and stabilises the nitronium electrophile.
viva.commonMisconception: Thinking H2SO4 is merely a solvent for the reaction.

viva.question: Why is the acetamido (-NHCOCH3) group used instead of a free amine (-NH2) for this nitration?
viva.expectedConcept: A free -NH2 group is so strongly activating and easily oxidised that direct nitration of aniline gives extensive oxidation and tar. Acetylating it first moderates its activating power (still ortho/para-directing, but far less reactive), allowing a controlled, cleaner mononitration.
viva.answerLogic: Acetylation protects and moderates the amine for controlled nitration.
viva.commonMisconception: Assuming the acetyl group has no electronic effect, only a protective one.

preLab.question: Recrystallisation is expected to:
options: Lower the yield but increase the purity
Increase the yield but lower the purity
Change the product into a different compound
preLab.feedback: Some product is always lost in the mother liquor during recrystallisation, but what remains is purer, shown by a sharper, higher melting point.

duringLab.question: Complete the preparation and record both crude and purified yield.

postLab.question: State the melting point of the purified product (°C).

scientificValidation.formula: % yield = (obtained/theoretical) × 100; melting point as purity check
assumptions: Reaction goes to a realistic, not complete, conversion
One recrystallisation removes most but not all impurity
edgeCases: Poor cooling during an exothermic step lowers both yield and purity
expectedBehaviour: Purified yield < crude yield; purified m.p. closer to literature value
